policies.title: Panama: named ordinary passports visa-exempt with Tourist Card
policies.summary: Executive Decree 326 expressly exempts these nationalities from a Panama visa for tourist entry. The same decree requires the National Migration Service to issue the corresponding Tourist Card; the card is a separate document and fee, not an ETA, eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: Decree 326 expressly removes the visa requirement for the named nationals entering as tourists and directs the National Migration Service to issue the corresponding Tourist Card.
The Tourist Card costs B/.50.00 under the decree. It is not classified here as an ETA, eVisa, visa on arrival or advance visa.

The live Foreign Ministry portal confirms that the applicable authorized visa, stamped visa or Tourist Card depends on the traveller’s country, but it does not publish a current nationality schedule or confirm that every 2012 named row remains unamended; this policy therefore remains medium confidence.

The authority’s general tourist page requires entry through an authorized post, a valid travel document, an entry/exit card or automated equivalent, no entry impediment and applicable funds, return travel and health conditions.

The source does not establish a current residual rule for unlisted nationalities; no complement is inferred. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Panama: Russian ordinary passports visa-exempt
policies.summary: The National Migration Service’s official 2014 decree index says Executive Decree 201 excludes the Russian Federation from the consular-stamped-visa countries and includes it among nationalities that do not need a visa to enter Panama.
conditions: This is a visa exemption, not an ETA, eVisa, visa on arrival or Tourist Card classification.
The source does not state duration, entries, fee, extension, return/onward travel, funds, accommodation, health or admission outcome for this route; none is inferred.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Panama: named ordinary passports require stamped consular visa
policies.summary: Current official Migration Service material expressly places China, India and Venezuela in a stamped-visa process. This is an advance consular visa baseline, not an eVisa, ETA or visa on arrival.
conditions: China is included in the countries whose nationals require a Panamanian consular stamped visa; the official notice describes consular security verification.

India is included in the countries requiring a visa stamped by the consul. Venezuela’s 2022 decree requires a stamped visa at the Panamanian consular office in the country where the traveller is located.
Online appointment or visa-in-line procedures facilitate a stamped-visa application; they do not establish an eVisa status.

The conditional waiver for holders of specified third-country visas or residence documents is excluded and does not alter this nationality-only baseline. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service and special-document routes are also excluded.

policies.title: Panama: named ordinary passports require authorized visa
policies.summary: The Migration Service’s official decree indexes place Haiti and Kosovo among nationalities requiring prior authorization to enter. The Foreign Ministry distinguishes an authorized visa as a consular visa issued after National Migration Service authorization; it is normalized as visa_required.
conditions: The policy is an advance authorized-visa process, not an eVisa, ETA or visa on arrival.
The Foreign Ministry says a consul grants an authorized visa only after authorization by the National Migration Service.
No online application, third-country document, purpose-specific exception, fee, duration, entries, extension, return/onward travel, funds, accommodation, health or admission outcome is inferred.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service and special-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Panama: Cuba and Dominican Republic ordinary passports require advance visa
policies.summary: Executive Decree 611 places Cuba and the Dominican Republic in the stamped-visa cohort; the 2021 decree removed their Tourist Card route. The current SNM notice confirms Cuba’s stamped-visa process.
conditions: This is an advance-visa baseline. The underlying legal materials distinguish stamped and authorised visas, but both are normalized as visa_required rather than electronic or arrival access.
A current eligible third-country visa or residence can waive the Panamanian visa under Decree 521 conditions; it is not a passport-only exemption and is not normalized here.

Tourist conditions include a valid travel document, financial means, onward travel where required, health/security checks and final immigration admission. Work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service and other special-document routes are outside scope.
